A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GBRL work by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original GBRL-versus-NN experiments across control, Football, Atari RAM and MiniGrid environments, together with library-throughput and shared-architecture experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds variable-isolation experiments, distribution-shift evaluations, feature-attribution analyses and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions grow ensembles from actor-critic gradients, share actor/critic tree structures and use distinct output learning rates with PPO, A2C and AWR. v2 documents and compares gradient-normalization and cosine split-scoring options, but does not establish a revision to the underlying procedure; these additions concern implementation disclosure and ablation evidence.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark coverage and adds three linear-equation variable-isolation tasks. Section 5.2 also introduces distinct MiniGrid correlation and distractor scenarios, noisy control observations, and Football scenarios with missing opponents, substantially expanding task and input-environment coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated external comparators remain NN implementations of PPO, A2C and AWR, plus CatBoost and XGBoost. A2C/AWR comparisons remain in the appendices despite the main text's PPO focus. The new experiments extend existing comparator families rather than introduce additional baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds cross-condition training/testing, 100-episode noisy evaluations with variance from 0 to 0.2, asymmetric training budgets for variable isolation and distractors, controlled CartPole parameter sweeps, and a synthetic incremental-learning timing protocol. Original benchmark budgets and tabulated hyperparameters are retained. For the aggregate plot, v2 Section 5.1 substitutes the earlier per-environment difference formula for v1 Figure 1's ratio normalization, leaving the plotted normalization ambiguous.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained shared-versus-separate architecture experiment, v2 adds tests of spurious correlations, distractors, observation noise and missing opponents, with a SHAP case study examining feature reliance. Section 6 and Appendices A–B add sensitivity analyses for actor/critic learning rates, tree depth, batch size, split scoring and updates per rollout.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and means with standard deviations. v2 makes this more explicit in retained table and learning-curve captions and extends the practice to new experiments, without reporting increased run counts, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 2–5 and v2 Tables 3–6 contain identical benchmark values, and the four appendix learning-curve images are retained. New results nevertheless substantially expand the evidence: Figures 5–15 report variable-isolation performance, robustness, feature attribution and sensitivity findings. New Table 1 reports incremental-learning times of 5.47 seconds for GBRL, 36.17 for CatBoost and 67.11 for XGBoost under its specified workload.

T1.justification: The gradient-fitting target changes from -epsilon times the gradient in v1 Equation (2) to the unscaled negative gradient in v2 Equation (1), while learning-rate scaling remains in the ensemble update. This removes an extra scaling factor from the mathematical presentation. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims viable GBT-based actor-critic learning, structured-data advantages and an efficient shared architecture, motivated partly by interpretability and edge deployment. v2 retains the framework claims but makes superior OOD robustness, resistance to spurious correlations and handling of state perturbations an explicit central contribution. The earlier interpretability and low-compute deployment emphasis is substantially reduced.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking tree partitions to preservation of rare reward signals, SHAP feature reliance to resistance against misleading cues, and threshold-based predictions to noise robustness. It also develops explanations of convergence/runtime tradeoffs and algorithm-dependent update frequency. The principal limitations concerning ensemble growth and nondifferentiable Q-functions are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the NN's two 64-unit tanh layers and separate output heads, GAE and critic-loss details, the depth-4 choice, and actor/critic split-scoring alternatives. Appendix C and Table 2 document the new variable-isolation environment and its hyperparameters. These materially expand reproducibility information, although v1's Algorithm 1 and some traditional-library setup details disappear. Hardware disclosures and repository access remain.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around tabular inductive biases and OOD behavior, adding works such as Jeffares et al., Beyazit et al. and Xu et al., while removing the dedicated interpretability discussion and several associated references. It also explicitly positions GBRL as extending NPPG beyond discrete Gibbs policies to general actor-critic objectives, replacing the earlier broader functional-policy-search discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. Standard experiments are consolidated, library and shared-architecture comparisons move into Section 4.3, and A2C/AWR explanations move to the appendix. The standard/challenge experiment structure and reordered conclusion and limitations substantially change the presentation beyond simply adding scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. The framework diagram and overview plots are redrawn, v1's per-environment comparison Figures 3–5 disappear while their underlying results remain, and v2 adds a timing table plus extensive robustness, SHAP and ablation graphics. Retained appendix tables and curves are resized, relocated and recaptioned.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly established benchmark viability and inferred advantages from structured-data performance. v2 directly probes robustness through controlled changes to correlations, noise and opponent availability, and adds sensitivity/runtime studies that substantially improve evidence about when GBRL works and how to configure it. The implementation disclosures further improve reproducibility. Removal of pseudocode and ambiguity in Figure 4's normalization are drawbacks, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
